Fashion / Style notes

Let texture do the talking

Build interest with the surface, weight, and feel of a piece.

✳
The Offbeat EditCulture Issue · 1 min read

IN THIS STORY

Begin with contrastKeep the proportions simpleWork with what you haveMore from Fashion

Begin with contrast

A smooth shirt and a textured knit can make a simple outfit feel considered. Rather than adding more colours, try noticing the difference between matte, crisp, soft, and structured surfaces.

Look at the pieces in daylight if possible. Texture can read differently under a shop’s lighting, and comfort matters as much as the photograph.

Keep the proportions simple

Choose one piece to carry most of the texture and let the others give it space. If several layers feel busy together, remove one before adding another.

Move in the combination before deciding. A fabric that looks appealing while standing still may bunch, catch, or feel too warm in an ordinary day.

Work with what you have

Revisit a jacket or scarf you have stopped noticing. Pairing it with a familiar base can reveal a useful contrast without changing the whole wardrobe.

The point is a set of combinations you enjoy wearing. No single fabric or formula is required to make an outfit your own.

“Build interest with the surface, weight, and feel of a piece.”
